source: Interim team, hand-written per CLAUDE.md §3.2. Seriousness wording follows ICH E2A (hospitalization or prolongation of hospitalization is a seriousness criterion).
rationale: Three non-PRO-CTCAE gate questions close every check-in: a seriousness trigger (hospital/ER), a concomitant-medication capture whose text is stored verbatim and matched only by string distance, and a free-text field that is stored verbatim and never parsed (it can only raise a 'read by a human' flag together with a severe item). The optional typed temperature belongs to the fever item but is captured with the gates so the kiosk can ask it on the same screen.

questions.label: Since your last study visit, were you admitted to a hospital or seen in an emergency room?
Since your last study visit, have you started or stopped any medication? This includes over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and supplements.
questions.text_prompt: Please type the name of the medication as it appears on the label.
questions.text_note: Stored exactly as typed. A deterministic string matcher proposes a normalized name; a coordinator confirms it.
questions.direction_prompt: Did you start it, stop it, or both?

questions.label: Is there anything else you would like the study team to know?
questions.note: Stored verbatim and never parsed by software. It is read by a person.

optional_fields.label: If you took your temperature, what was the highest reading? (optional)
